facts.statement: The genus Revueltosaurus was described by Adrian P. Hunt in 1989.
facts.quote: authority: Hunt, 1989

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus lived during the Late Triassic, from the late Carnian to the middle Norian stages, in what is now New Mexico, Arizona, and North Carolina.
facts.quote: Late Triassic (late Carnian to middle Norian stage) deposits of New Mexico, Arizona and North Carolina, United States

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus was approximately 1 meter (3.3 feet) in length.
facts.quote: Revueltosaurus was about 1 meter (3.3 feet) long

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus callenderi is the type species of the genus, named by Adrian P. Hunt in 1989.
facts.quote: R. callenderi was named by Adrian P. Hunt in 1989 and it is the type species of the genus

facts.statement: The genus name Revueltosaurus honors the type locality, Revuelto Creek in Quay County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: The generic name honors its type locality, Revuelto Creek, Quay County of New Mexico

facts.statement: The name Revueltosaurus derives from the Spanish word for 'revolution', referencing the Late Triassic period's importance to terrestrial vertebrate evolution.
facts.quote: Revuelto is derived from Spanish revuelta, "revolution", in reference to the importance of the Late Triassic period for terrestrial vertebrate evolution

facts.statement: The species name callenderi honors Jonathan F. Callender, the director of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the director of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History Jonathan F. Callender

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus callenderi is found in the early-mid Norian Bull Canyon Formation in New Mexico and the Norian Chinle Formation in Arizona.
facts.quote: R. callenderi is known to date only from the Revueltian (early-mid Norian, the type locality dates back to the early Norian) of Bull Canyon Formation (Dockum Group, New Mexico) and the Painted Desert of the Petrified Forest Member (Chinle Formation, Arizona)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that osteoderms at the end of the tail may have formed a tail club.
facts.quote: It is also thought that the osteoderms on the end of the tail form a "tail club."

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus hunti was named by Andrew B. Heckert in 2002, originally classified as a basal ornithischian.
facts.quote: R. hunti was named by Andrew B. Heckert in 2002 as a basal ornithischian

facts.statement: The species name hunti honors paleontologist Adrian P. Hunt for his contributions to Triassic studies.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the paleontologist Adrian P. Hunt for his contributions to the Triassic paleontology

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus hunti lived during the latest Carnian stage.
facts.quote: dating to the latest Carnian stage (Adamanian)

facts.statement: Parker et al. (2005) suggested that R. hunti is a pseudosuchian based on a squamosal bone nearly identical to that of R. callenderi.
facts.quote: Parker et al. (2005) confirmed that R. hunti may be assignable to Revueltosaurus, on the basis of undescribed squamosal collected from its referred locality that is nearly identical to that seen in the Petrified Forest material of R. callenderi, thus suggesting that R. hunti is a pseudosuchian

facts.statement: Irmis et al. (2007) and Nesbitt et al. (2007) synonymized Krzyzanowskisaurus with Revueltosaurus, arguing that its dental features are unique to R. hunti and not related to ornithischians or mammals.
facts.quote: Irmis et al. (2007) and Nesbitt et al. (2007) synonymized Krzyzanowskisaurus with Revueltosaurus, and argued that this condition of the dentation is an autapomorphy of R. hunti and is not homologous to the ornithischian asymmetric swelling or a mammalian cingulum

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus olseni was originally named Pekinosaurus by Hunt and Lucas in 1994 as a basal ornithischian.
facts.quote: R. olseni was named by Hunt and Lucas in 1994 as a basal ornithischian, under the generic name Pekinosaurus

facts.statement: The original genus name Pekinosaurus honors Pekin, North Carolina, the type locality.
facts.quote: The generic name honors Pekin, North Carolina, where its type series was collected

facts.statement: The species name olseni honors paleontologist Paul E. Olsen.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the paleontologist Paul E. Olsen

facts.statement: Recent studies indicate that the strata containing R. olseni at the Moncure locality are likely early Norian in age.
facts.quote: Most recent work, however, demonstrates that much of it is in fact Norian in age. Therefore, the strata exposed at the Moncure locality are probably early Norian in age

facts.statement: Irmis et al. (2007) and Nesbitt et al. (2007) tentatively synonymized Pekinosaurus with Revueltosaurus, noting the lack of unique diagnostic features in the original description.
facts.quote: Irmis et al. (2007) and Nesbitt et al. (2007) tentatively synonymized Pekinosaurus (and Galtonia) with Revueltosaurus, and refer its type series to Revueltosaurus sp. They noted that Hunt and Lucas (1994) did not provide any differential diagnosis, autapomorphies, or unique combination of characters for Pekinosaurus

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus is an extinct genus of suchian pseudosuchian.
facts.quote: Revueltosaurus ("Revuelto lizard") is an extinct genus of suchian pseudosuchian

facts.statement: Nearly the entire skeleton of R. callenderi is known, with a full description currently being prepared.
facts.quote: Thus, nearly the entire skeleton of R. callenderi is known and a full description of it is being prepared

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus is an extinct pseudosuchian archosaur from the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Revueltosaurus (de la localidad de Revuelto Creek, en Estados Unidos, y del griego latinizado saurus 'lagarto') es un género extinto de arcosaurio suquio pseudosuquio del Triásico Superior

facts.statement: Fossils of Revueltosaurus have been found in the US states of New Mexico, Arizona, and North Carolina.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles se hallan en los estados de Nuevo México, Arizona y Carolina del Norte, en los Estados Unidos

facts.statement: The species R. callenderi was named by Adrian P. Hunt in 1989 as the type species of the genus.
facts.quote: R. callenderi fue nombrado por Adrian P. Hunt en 1989 y es el tipo nomenclatural del género

facts.statement: The genus name honors its type locality, Revuelto Creek in Quay County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: El nombre del género fue puesto en honor a su localidad tipo, Revuelto Creek, del condado de Quay en Nuevo México en Estados Unidos

facts.statement: The specific name honors Jonathan F. Callender, the director of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra el director del Museo de Historia Natural y Ciencia de Nuevo México, Jonathan F. Callender

facts.statement: R. callenderi was originally described as a basal ornithischian based on 32 teeth.
facts.quote: R. callenderi fue descrito originalmente como un ornitisquio basal basándose en 32 dientes

facts.statement: Andrew B. Heckert named the second species, R. hunti, in 2002 based on teeth described by Hunt and Lucas in 1994.
facts.quote: Andrew B. Heckert (2002) redescribe del género en detalle y nombró una segunda especie, R. hunti basándose en los dientes descritos por Hunt y Lucas (1994)

facts.statement: Parker and colleagues described several partial skeletons of R. callenderi, including nearly complete skulls, from the Revueltosaurus Quarry in Petrified Forest National Park in 2005.
facts.quote: Parker et al. (2005) describieron varios esqueletos parcialmente completos de R. callenderi (PEFO 33787-95), incluyendo unos cráneos casi completos y parciales, de la Cantera Revueltosaurus, en el Parque nacional del Bosque Petrificado

facts.statement: Sterling J. Nesbitt noted in 2011 that much of the cranial and postcranial material of Revueltosaurus comes from a monospecific bonebed.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con Sterling J. Nesbitt (2011), gran parte del material craneal y postcraneal de Revueltosaurus se origina a partir de un lecho de huesos monotípico

facts.statement: New skeletal discoveries suggest that Revueltosaurus is a pseudosuchian rather than an ornithischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: New discoveries of skeletal material of R. callenderi have suggested that Revueltosaurus is a pseudosuchian

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Revueltosaurus at the base of the clade Suchia as the sister taxon to armored aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Revueltosaurus was placed at the base of the clade Suchia as the sister taxon to the armored and herbivorous aetosaurs

facts.statement: The genus includes three species: R. callenderi (type species), R. olseni, and R. hunti.
facts.quote: subdivision: †R. callenderi Hunt, 1989 (especie tipo) †R. olseni (Hunt & Lucas, 1994) †R. hunti Heckert, 2002

facts.statement: Krzyzanowskisaurus and Pekinosaurus are synonyms of Revueltosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Krzyzanowskisaurus (Heckert, 2002) Pekinosaurus Hunt & Lucas, 1994

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether dentition alone can reliably identify early dinosaurs, noting that Revueltosaurus teeth resemble those of herbivorous ornithischians despite the animal being a pseudosuchian.
facts.quote: because the teeth look like those we know from herbivorous ornithischians, people assigned them to the dinosaurs. We think we've shown that you can't rely on the dentition to determine what is an early dinosaur

facts.statement: Heckert erected the genus Krzyzanowskisaurus for R. hunti in 2005, suggesting its denticulated tooth enamel represented a cingulum.
facts.quote: Heckert (2005) erigió un nuevo género para R. hunti, Krzyzanowskisaurus. Él sugirió que la coraza denticulada en los dientes representaba un cíngulo

facts.statement: Irmis et al. and Nesbitt et al. synonymized Krzyzanowskisaurus with Revueltosaurus, arguing the tooth condition is an autapomorphy of R. hunti and not homologous to ornithischian asymmetry or mammalian cingula.
facts.quote: Irmis et al. (2007) y Nesbitt et al. (2007) sinonimizaron a Krzyzanowskisaurus con Revueltosaurus, y argumentaron que esta condición de la dentación es una autapomorfía de R. hunti y no es homóloga a la inflamación asimétrica de los ornitisquios o al cíngulo de los mamíferos

facts.statement: Nearly the entire skeleton of R. callenderi is known, prompting the preparation of a complete description.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, casi todo el esqueleto del R. callenderi es conocido, por lo que se está preparando una descripción completa del mismo

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus olseni was originally named in 1994 by Hunt and Lucas under the genus name Pekinosaurus.
facts.quote: R. olseni fue nombrado por Hunt y Lucas en 1994 como un ornitisquio basal, bajo el nombre de género Pekinosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the locality of Pekin in North Carolina where the type series was collected.
facts.quote: El nombre del género honra a la localidad de Pekin, en Carolina del Norte, donde se recogió su serie tipo.

facts.statement: Hunt and Lucas named the genus based on the tooth series YPM 7666-9.
facts.quote: Hunt y Lucas nombraron al género basándose en la serie de dientes YPM 7666-9.

facts.statement: Although Hunt and Lucas designated YPM 8545 as the holotype, Heckert et al. (2012) determined the correct holotype is YPM 7666.
facts.quote: Se debe señalar que ellos designaron como holotipo a YPM 8545, pero la denominación correcta es YPM 7666 de acuerdo con Heckert et al. (2012).

facts.statement: The Cumnock Formation, where the type locality is found, belongs to the Chathan Group and is recognized as Late Triassic.
facts.quote: La Formación Cumnock pertenece al Grupo Chathan (del supergrupo Newark), que es reconocido como del Triásico Superior.

facts.statement: Most researchers have assigned the Cumnock Formation to the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los investigadores han asignado la Formación Cumnock al Carniense.

facts.statement: Recent work demonstrates that much of the Cumnock Formation is actually from the Norian stage.
facts.quote: El trabajo más reciente, sin embargo, demuestra que gran parte de ella es de hecho del Noriense.

facts.statement: Therefore, the exposed strata at the Moncure locality are likely from the early Norian.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, los estratos expuestos en la localidad Moncure son probablemente de principios del Noriense.

facts.statement: R. olseni is thought to have been one of the most common tetrapods in its faunal zone.
facts.quote: Se piensa que R. olseni era uno de los tetrápodos más comunes en su zona faunística.

facts.statement: New skeletal discoveries of R. callenderi suggest that Revueltosaurus was a pseudosuchian.
facts.quote: Nuevos descubrimientos de material esquelético de R. callenderi han sugerido que Revueltosaurus era un pseudosuquio.

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus is placed at the base of the clade Suchia as the sister taxon to armored and herbivorous aetosaurs.
facts.quote: A Revueltosaurus se lo coloca en la base del clado Suchia como el taxón hermano de los aetosaurios blindados y herbívoros.

facts.statement: However, Revueltosaurus is not an aetosaur because the group Aetosauria was redefined to exclude it.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Revueltosaurus no es un aetosaurio, ya que el grupo Aetosauria fue redefinido para excluirlo.

facts.statement: Revueltosaurus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Revueltosaurus as Aetosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Aetosauria

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Revueltosaurus is Revueltosaurus callenderi.
facts.quote: Type species: Revueltosaurus callenderi

rejected.statement: The name 'Revuelto' derives from the Spanish word for 'revolution', referencing the importance of the Late Triassic in terrestrial vertebrate evolution.
rejected.quote: El nombre «Revuelto» a su vez se deriva de la palabra española «revuelta», que es sinónimo de 'revolución', en referencia a la importancia del período Triásico Superior en la evolución de los vertebrados terrestres
